source_refs.note: Book p. 263-264: heading printed 14.1.7; properties (i)-(vi), proofs of (i)-(iv). Book error: (iii) printed u + 0 = 0. Proofs of (v), (vi), teaching notes, Key points, Common mistakes are ours.

blocks.title: Numbering note
blocks.text: Kitab is heading ko 14.1.7 chhaapti hai (Book# 14.1.7). Kitab mein 14.1.1 naam ki koi heading hai hi nahin, is liye portal 14.1 ke sub-headings ko tarteeb se 14.1.1 se 14.1.8 tak number karta hai. Yahan 14.1.6 wahi hai jo kitab mein 14.1.7 hai.

Bachon, numbers ke saath aap ne bohat se qaide parhe hain: \(2 + 3 = 3 + 2\), \(5 + 0 = 5\), \(7 + (-7) = 0\). Is subtopic mein hum dekhenge ke vectors bhi jama aur scalar se zarb mein bilkul inhi qaidon par chalte hain. Yeh baat isliye ahem hai ke aage vector equations hal karte waqt hum yeh qaide bila jhijhak istemaal karenge. Proofs ka tareeqa bhi ek hi hai, is liye ek samajh gaye to sab samajh aa jaayenge.
Farz karein \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) plane ya space ke vectors hain aur \(a, b \in R\), to un ke yeh properties hain:

blocks.caption: Vectors ke properties (plane ya space), a, b real numbers

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab property (iii) ko \(\underline{u} + \underline{0} = \underline{0}\) chhaapti hai. Zero vector jama karne se vector nahin badalta, is liye sahi \(\underline{u} + \underline{0} = \underline{u}\) (Additive Identity) hai; kitab ka apna proof bhi neeche yahi nateeja deta hai. Table mein humne sahi likha hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh chhe qaide kehte hain ke jama aur number se zarb mein vectors aam numbers jaisa bartaao karte hain. Har proof ka tareeqa ek hi hai: vectors ko components mein likhiye, har component par real numbers wala wahi qaida lagaiye, aur components ko wapas jor dijiye.
Kyun yeh kaam karta hai: vector ka jama component ba component hota hai, aur har component ek aam real number hai. Jo qaida real numbers mein sach hai, woh har component mein sach hai, is liye poore vector mein bhi sach hai.
Proof

(i) Kisi bhi do real numbers \(a, b \in R\) ke liye \(a + b = b + a\) hota hai. Is se nikalta hai ke \(R^{3}\) ke kisi bhi do vectors \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) aur \(\underline{v} = [x', y', z']\) ke liye bhi yahi sach hai, jin ke components \(R\) mein hain.

blocks.text_alt: u plus v equals x, y, z plus x prime, y prime, z prime
equals x plus x prime and so on

blocks.latex: = [x' + x,\ y' + y,\ z' + z] \quad \because a + b = b + a
blocks.text_alt: equals x prime plus x and so on, because a plus b equals b plus a

blocks.text: Is liye \(R^{3}\) mein vectors ka jama commutative hai (tarteeb badalne se jawab nahin badalta).

(ii) Kisi bhi teen real numbers \(a, b, c \in R\) ke liye \((a + b) + c = a + (b + c)\). Is se nikalta hai ke \(R^{3}\) ke kisi bhi teen vectors \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\), \(\underline{v} = [x', y', z']\) aur \(\underline{w} = [x'', y'', z'']\) ke liye, jin ke components \(R\) mein hain:

blocks.latex: (\underline{u} + \underline{v}) + \underline{w} \\ = [x + x',\ y + y',\ z + z'] + [x'', y'', z'']
blocks.text_alt: u plus v, plus w, equals x plus x prime and so on, plus x double prime and so on
equals x plus x prime, plus x double prime, and so on
equals x plus, x prime plus x double prime, and so on

blocks.latex: = [x, y, z] + [x' + x'',\ y' + y'',\ z' + z''] \\ = \underline{u} + (\underline{v} + \underline{w})
blocks.text_alt: equals u plus, v plus w

blocks.text: Is liye \(R^{3}\) mein vectors ka jama associative hai (pehle kin do ko jama karein, is se farq nahin parta).

(iii) Kisi bhi real number \(a\) aur 0 ke liye \(a + 0 = a\). Is se nikalta hai ke kisi bhi vector \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) aur \(\underline{0} = [0, 0, 0]\) ke liye, jahan \(\underline{0}\) \(R^{3}\) ka zero vector hai:

blocks.text_alt: u plus zero vector equals x, y, z plus 0, 0, 0
equals x plus 0 and so on equals u
u plus zero vector equals u

blocks.text: Is liye \(\underline{0}\) \(R^{3}\) mein additive identity hai.

(iv) Har real number \(a\) ke liye ek \(-a\) hota hai jis se \(a + (-a) = a - a = 0\). Is se nikalta hai ke har vector \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) ke liye \(R^{3}\) mein \(-\underline{u} = [-x, -y, -z]\) maujood hai, aisa ke

blocks.text_alt: u plus minus u equals x, y, z plus minus x, minus y, minus z
equals x plus minus x and so on
u plus minus u equals zero vector

blocks.text: Is liye \(-\underline{u}\) \(R^{3}\) mein \(\underline{u}\) ka additive inverse hai.
Baaqi hisson ke proofs kitab ne students ke liye exercise ke taur par chhor diye hain (neeche hum ne kar ke dikhaye hain).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
(v) ka proof: \(\underline{v} = [x', y', z']\), \(\underline{w} = [x'', y'', z'']\), \(a \in R\) lein.
\[a(\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = a[x' + x'',\ y' + y'',\ z' + z'']\]
\[= [ax' + ax'',\ ay' + ay'',\ az' + az'']\]
\[= [ax', ay', az'] + [ax'', ay'', az''] = a\underline{v} + a\underline{w}\]
Kyun: doosri line mein har component par real numbers ka distributive qaida \(a(p + q) = ap + aq\) laga hai.
(vi) ka proof: \(a(b\underline{u}) = a[bx, by, bz] = [abx, aby, abz] = (ab)[x, y, z] = (ab)\underline{u}\), kyunke real numbers mein \(a(bx) = (ab)x\) hota hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Kya \(\underline{u} - \underline{v} = \underline{v} - \underline{u}\) hota hai? \(\underline{u} = [1, 2, 3]\), \(\underline{v} = [0, 1, 1]\) le kar dekhiye.
Jawab: \(\underline{u} - \underline{v} = [1, 1, 2]\) aur \(\underline{v} - \underline{u} = [-1, -1, -2]\). Barabar nahin, balke ek doosre ke negative hain. Yani minus commutative nahin, bilkul numbers ki tarah (\(5 - 3\) aur \(3 - 5\) alag hain).

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Proof likhte waqt har aham qadam ke saath wajah likhiye, jaise \(\because a + b = b + a\). Examiner yahi dekhta hai ke aap ne real numbers wala qaida kahan istemaal kiya. Sirf \(\underline{u} + \underline{v} = \underline{v} + \underline{u}\) likh dena proof nahin, yeh to wahi baat dohraana hai jo saabit karni thi.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
Vectors ka jama commutative aur associative hai.
\(\underline{0}\) additive identity hai: \(\underline{u} + \underline{0} = \underline{u}\).
\(-\underline{u}\) additive inverse hai: \(\underline{u} + (-\underline{u}) = \underline{0}\).
Scalar jama par phailta hai aur aapas mein zarb hota hai: \(a(\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = a\underline{v} + a\underline{w}\), \(a(b\underline{u}) = (ab)\underline{u}\).
Har proof component wise real numbers ke qaide par aata hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
\(\underline{u} + \underline{0} = \underline{0}\) likh dena (kitab ki misprint ki tarah), ya \(\underline{u} - \underline{u}\) ka jawab vector \(\underline{0}\) ki jagah number 0 likhna.
Proof mein components dikhaaye baghair seedha \(\underline{u} + \underline{v}\) se \(\underline{v} + \underline{u}\) par chhalaang lagana.
Aham qadam ki wajah (real numbers wala qaida) na likhna.
